transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

# Bosch E:15: Water in the Base (Anti-Flood Protection)

E:15 means the Aquastop/anti-flood system has detected water in the base tray under the machine. A float switch has lifted, so the dishwasher runs the drain pump nonstop to prevent a flood. Turning it off and on won't clear it. The water has to be removed and the float has to drop.

## Step 1: Make it safe
1. Switch off at the wall and unplug (or turn off at the isolator/fuse spur).
2. Turn off the water supply to the dishwasher.

## Step 2: Get the water out of the base
On a fully integrated model like yours, the float sits in a plastic tray under the tub.

Option A: Soak it out (least effort)
• Remove the kickplate/plinth at the bottom (usually a few screws or clips).
• Look for water in the base tray and soak it up with towels or a sponge. A wet/dry vac works well if you can reach.

Option B: Tilt it (more thorough)
• Unscrew the mounting brackets from the worktop/cabinet sides.
• Slide the machine partly out, being careful with the hoses and cable.
• With a helper, tilt it back about 45° so the water runs out of the tray. Have towels ready.
• Don't tip it fully on its back.

Then let it dry. Leave it unplugged for 24 hours, or use a hairdryer on a cool/low setting around the base. The float must be fully free and dry.

## Step 3: Find out why water got there
If you skip this, E:15 will come straight back. Common causes:

| Cause | What to check |
|---|---|
| Too many suds (most common) | Was washing-up liquid, hand soap, or the wrong detergent used? Even a squirt on pre-rinsed dishes can cause it. Rinse aid overdosed or leaking? |
| Door seal | Inspect the rubber seal for splits, debris, or food stuck under it. |
| Overloading/blocked spray | Large items deflecting water out past the door. |
| Spray arms | Cracked arm, or arm not clipped on properly. |
| Filter | Blocked or badly seated filter. Clean and refit it firmly. |
| Internal leak | Hoses, sump seal, pump, or heater pump leaking. Look for drips or watermarks when it runs. |

## Step 4: Test it
• Plug back in, restore water, and run a short programme empty.
• If you can, leave the kickplate off and watch underneath with a torch for drips.

## When to call a technician
• E:15 returns after an empty test run with no suds involved.
• You can see water leaking from the pump, hoses, or sump area.
• The base keeps refilling.

Bosch customer service or an engineer can replace the leaking part. If the machine is under 2 years old (or has an extended warranty), contact Bosch before dismantling anything.

Was anything different about the last wash, such as a new detergent, a heavy load, or hand-washed items going in with soap on them? That would help narrow it down.

I can't pull it out or tilt it, it's fully integrated under the worktop and the plinth is glued at the ends. I can see a bit of shine from water in the base tray through a gap with a torch. Filter is fairly clean, door seal looks ok, and I use tablets so no suds. It's 3.5 years old so out of warranty.

# Clearing E:15 Without Pulling the Machine Out

Since you can see water in the tray, the error is genuine. You just need to get that water out and the float back down. Keep the machine unplugged while you work, both for safety and to stop the pump wearing itself out running nonstop.

## Getting the water out through the gap

Use whatever reaches best:

• Wick it out: Push strips of kitchen roll, a microfibre cloth, or a chamois into the tray with a thin ruler or a straightened coat hanger. Pull them out, wring, and repeat. It's slow but works well.
• Suck it out:
• A wet/dry vac with a length of narrow hose (aquarium tubing or similar) taped into the nozzle
• A large syringe or turkey baster with tubing on the end
• Dry what's left: Point a fan or a hairdryer on cool/low into the gap for a few hours, then leave it unplugged for 24 to 48 hours. The float only drops once the water level falls far enough, so even a small amount left can keep the error on.

Then plug in. If E:15 has gone, the float has dropped.

## Finding the leak

Tablets and a clean filter rule out the usual suspects, so on a 3.5-year-old Bosch the likely causes are:

1. The heat pump (the combined circulation pump and heater under the tub). Its seals and hose connections are a well-known leak point on Bosch/Siemens machines of this age.
2. The sump seal around the filter housing.
3. A hose clip or connection that has weeped, such as the drain hose, inlet, or the salt/softener unit.
4. The door or detergent dispenser. Look for drips running down the inside face of the door after a cycle.
5. Occasional suds, for example if someone rinsed dishes in washing-up water first, or the rinse aid is set too high or its cap is leaking.

A quick test once it's dry: Run a short cycle and stay nearby. Check the gap with your torch every 10 to 15 minutes, and also look under the door edge.
• If E:15 comes back quickly, it's an active leak (most likely the pump or a hose), and the machine will need to come out to fix it.
• If it takes several cycles to return, it's more likely a slow weep or an occasional suds problem.

## If it does need to come out

The plinth is the main obstacle:

• The glued ends are often just end caps or a bead of sealant. You can usually cut along the line with a sharp knife and then prise the plinth off the clips on the cabinet legs. A replacement plinth is cheap if it gets damaged.
• After that it's normally just two screws holding the machine to the underside of the worktop (or to the cabinet sides). Lower the feet slightly so it clears the worktop, and it should slide forward far enough to reach the base.

## Repair cost vs replacing

A heat pump or seal repair is usually worth doing on a machine of this age. Typical costs:

| Option | Rough cost |
|---|---|
| Heat pump part, DIY | £80–£150 |
| Fitted by an engineer | £150–£250 |
| Bosch's own fixed-price repair | Worth a quote, as it usually includes a warranty on the repair |

Some home insurance policies or extended appliance cover may also help.

If you'd like, tell me what you find during the test cycle (where the drips are, how fast the error returns) and I can help narrow down the part.
